newsitem.title: USA: ILEX to meet partner after FDA rejection.
newsitem.headline: ILEX to meet partner after FDA rejection.

text.p: ILEX Oncology Inc said on Monday that it will meet with its development partner Sanofi to set a new course of action, following a U.S. Food and Drug Administration panel's vote not to approve its Zyerkamine drug.

The FDA's Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee found that there was not substantial evidence that Zyrkamine was effective as a second-line treatment for patients with AIDS-related non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, the company said in a statement.
Sanofi has worldwide marketing rights to Zyerkamine under a licensing agreement with ILEX.

"While we respect the Committee's decision, we are disappointed and stand behind the demonstrated safety and efficacy of Zyrkamine," Richard Love, the company's president and chief executive said in a statement.
ILEX's shares fell 3-5/8 points to close at 14-1/2. The company's shares were halted mid-day before the FDA panel's decision.
ILEX said it has several promising compounds in development for treatment of cancers such as breast, bladder and chronic lymphocytic leukemia, as well as a growing contract research business.
ILEX submitted a new drug application (NDA) for Zyrkamine in October 1996 under the accelerated approval process set forth by the FDA for anticancer drugs.
Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, a cancer of the lymphatic system, is commonly associated with HIV infection and is the cause of death in 12-16 percent of patients with AIDS.
